title: Jude and the Oath
premise: Bram Vane, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, has spent three years selling small charms in a city that outlawed magic, hiding her gift and her grief. When a dying stranger presses a map into her unwilling hands, she discovers the stranger's soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain — and that her own dead mentor's oath is bound to the same debt. Joined by a disgraced cartographer and a runaway noble who knows the mountain's courts too well, Bram descends to steal the soul back before the long winter finishes falling and seals the underworld for a century. She succeeds only by speaking her final oath aloud, breaking her binding forever, and returns to find that family is not what you inherit but what you choose to keep.
about_author: Ansel Vasquez is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk ballads about bargains made in dark places. He writes fantasy from a small coastal town, where he claims the winter fog does half his plotting for him.

chapters.title: Charms for Copper
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. In the outlaw city of Greyhollow, Bram sells luck-knots and fever-charms while concealing the swordspeaker's oath burning under her skin. A market raid forces her to use magic to save a child, nearly exposing herself. Emotional beat: the exhaustion of hiding who you are.

chapters.title: The Dying Stranger
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A frostbitten woman collapses at Bram's stall, presses a bloodstained map into her hands, and whispers that her soul was 'sold beneath.' Watchmen arrive; the stranger dies smiling. Emotional beat: unwanted inheritance, guilt at being chosen.

chapters.title: What the Map Shows
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Studying the map in her cellar, Bram recognizes her dead mentor's handwriting woven into its borders — proof he knew the court beneath the mountain. The oath on her arm begins to ache toward the north. Emotional beat: grief reopened.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile Fen, a disgraced royal cartographer, recognizes the map as one she was forced to forge years ago. She tracks Bram down, offering honesty in exchange for passage out of the city before the watch finds them both. Emotional beat: two liars negotiating trust.

chapters.title: Outlaw Road
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Fleeing through the northern passes ahead of the early snows, Bram and Odile are ambushed by bounty hunters selling 'unregistered practitioners.' Bram speaks her first true sword-word in three years and hates how good it feels. Emotional beat: power as temptation.

chapters.title: The Runaway Lord
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. They find Cassian Merrow bleeding in a shrine, a noble's son who fled after learning his family sold his sister's soul to the mountain court generations ago. He carries the second half of the map. Emotional beat: found family's first fragile bond.

chapters.title: Winter's First Teeth
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Snowbound in an abandoned waystation, the three trade stories by firelight — Bram's mentor, Odile's forgery, Cassian's sister Liss. The map's ink shifts when they sleep, showing paths none of them drew. Emotional beat: warmth against the cold, and unease.

chapters.title: The Village That Remembers
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. In a mountain village, elders recognize the swordspeaker's mark and reveal the oath's origin: it was sworn to guard the door beneath the mountain, not to open it. Bram learns her mentor broke faith with the court. Emotional beat: legacy as burden.

chapters.title: Hunters on the Slope
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Court agents — the Hollow Wardens — ambush the party on a glacier crossing. Cassian freezes, unable to fight men wearing his house's colors; Odile saves him at cost of her hand frostbitten badly. Emotional beat: cowardice faced honestly.

chapters.title: The Door Beneath
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. They reach the sealed gate carved with her oath's words. Speaking it opens the way — but the mountain takes a toll: it shows Bram a vision of her mentor alive, bargaining below. Emotional beat: hope weaponized against her.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The party enters the underworld's upper galleries, where sold souls work endless looms weaving the long winter itself. Odile maps their route obsessively, terrified that if she stops drawing she'll forget the sky. Emotional beat: fear of erasure.

chapters.title: The Loom Hall
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Among the soul-weavers, Cassian finds Liss — alive, but thread-thin, her memories unraveling into cloth. She doesn't know him. He lies to her gently, saying he's a buyer. Emotional beat: love that cannot announce itself.

chapters.title: Audience with the Pale Court
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Summoned before the court beneath the mountain, Bram bargains for Liss's soul. The Pale Regent offers instead to restore her mentor and forgive her oath — if she leaves the others. Emotional beat: duty dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: The Bargain Refused
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram refuses, learning the truth: her mentor didn't break faith — he tried to buy back every stolen soul and failed, and the court kept his payment as leverage over her all along. Emotional beat: rage transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Threads Cut
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. The court, angered, begins unweaving Liss entirely. Cassian confesses who he is; in her last clear hour, Liss tells him where the master spindle hides. The party scatters as wardens close in. Emotional beat: despair before the climb.

chapters.title: Odile's True Map
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Captured and interrogated, Odile offers a forged map of the spindle vault — her finest work — trading her freedom for the others' escape. Alone in a cell, she draws the sky from memory on the floor. Emotional beat: sacrifice without applause.

chapters.title: The Spindle Vault
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Guided by Liss's directions, Bram and Cassian infiltrate the vault where the winter's pattern is anchored. Cassian holds the wardens while Bram reaches the spindle holding Liss's thread. Emotional beat: courage borrowed from each other.

chapters.title: The Oath Spoken
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. To cut the thread, Bram must speak her whole oath — which will burn out her magic forever. She speaks it, severs Liss's bond, and shatters the winter-loom as the mountain begins to fall. Emotional beat: giving up power to give back a life.

chapters.title: Collapse of the Long Winter
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The galleries crumble; Odile breaks free in the chaos, Cassian drags Liss toward the gate, and Bram — magicless and mortal — nearly drowns in falling snow-melt before her found family pulls her out. Emotional beat: no one escapes alone.

chapters.title: Above the Snowline
chapters.summary: Liss's POV. Waking in sunlight with a lifetime of missing memory, Liss must relearn her brother, her name, her grief. The village elders shelter the four fugitives as the unnatural winter breaks across the peaks. Emotional beat: slow, painful return.

chapters.title: Reckonings
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Back in Greyhollow, warrants are quietly withdrawn as the endless winter's cause becomes undeniable. Odile is restored to the cartographers' guild; Cassian renounces his title. Bram opens a shop that sells real charms, openly. Emotional beat: justice arriving imperfectly.

chapters.title: The Family Kept
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, epilogue. One year later, the four share a midwinter meal above the shop; Liss laughs at something Cassian says, and Bram's scarred arm aches only in cold weather. On the doorstep, a new stranger arrives carrying a map. Emotional beat: inheritance continues — but now it is chosen.
